He failed to score in China and finished seventh in Brazil, which allowed Ferrari's Kimi Raikkonen to pip both Hamilton and fellow McLaren driver Fernando Alonso by a single point. Somehow the climax to the 2008 championship, also in Brazil, was even more dramatic. Hamilton was battling for the title with Ferrari's home favourite Felipe Massa and the Briton's fourth place was going to be enough to secure the crown when a late rain shower changed everything. Leader Massa and Hamilton were among those who changed to intermediate tyres but Toyota's Timo Glock stayed out, which lifted him up to fourth. Hamilton, now in fifth, had Toro Rosso's Vettel right behind him and couldn't afford to lose another position. With just over two laps to go, he ran wide and Vettel was through. Massa crossed the line to win the race with Hamilton still sixth. The Ferrari pit crew, Massa's family and the Brazilian fans celebrated but with the rain intensifying, Glock was slowing on his dry-weather tyres and Hamilton passed him into the final corner to take the title by a single point. The Spaniard's speed and consistency ensured he prevailed over Raikkonen, whose McLaren-Mercedes was fast but fragile. A third place at the Brazilian Grand Prix was enough to give Alonso the title with two races to spare. He won a second consecutive title in 2006, also for Renault, and the 45-year-old remains one of the great personalities and outstanding talents in F1. He'll be back for another season with Aston Martin in 2027, 26 years after his debut for Minardi. His rival in a thrilling and intense season-long duel was Red Bull's Max Verstappen. There were plenty of flashpoints along the way and it all came to a climax in Abu Dhabi. Verstappen and Hamilton went into the final race of the season level on points. The Dutchman qualified on pole but Mercedes' Hamilton beat him off the line and largely controlled the race thereafter, until Williams' Nicholas Latifi crashed with five laps to go, bringing out a safety car. Hamilton did not have enough of an advantage over second-placed Verstappen to pit for fresh tyres and maintain the lead, so stayed out. Verstappen, with nothing to lose, came in and fitted softs. Race director Michael Masi allowed the lapped cars between Hamilton and Verstappen to go past, but not those behind the Red Bull. He allowed the race to restart for one final racing lap and Verstappen overtook Hamilton, who was a sitting duck on his old hard tyres. Verstappen and Hamilton, in their own ways, were both stunned and Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff shouted over the radio to Masi: "No, Michael, no! That was so not right!" As happened with Vettel from 2010-13, this was the first of four consecutive titles for a Red Bull driver with Verstappen dominating the 2022, 2023 and 2024 seasons. Emerson Fittipaldi Emerson Fittipaldi celebrates winning the 1972 Italian Grand Prix and the first of his two world titles [Getty Images] First championship: 1972 Age: 25 years and 273 days Stage of his F1 career when title was won: Second full season F1 debut: 1970 British Grand Prix (aged 23) Emerson Fittipaldi became the first Brazilian driver to win the F1 world title in 1972, with five wins from 12 races enough for the Lotus driver to get the better of Jackie Stewart. Fittipaldi would secure another drivers' title for McLaren two years later but his race-winning days, in F1 at least, were over once he joined his brother's Fittipaldi team in 1976. He would have late-career success in IndyCars, winning the 1989 title and the Indy 500 twice, in 1989 and 1993. He remained F1's youngest champion for 33 years until Alonso's first title ushered in an era where the record would change hands more regularly. item.title: Antonelli becomes world champion as Verstappen wins in Mexico
item.description: Kimi Antonelli did not win the race in Mexico City - but he did not need to [Getty Images] Kimi Antonelli clinched his first world title and became the youngest champion in Formula 1 history by finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Antonelli - 20 years and 68 days old - finished the race in third, behind Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton. His moment of glory came on a day when tensions at Ferrari between seven-time champion Hamilton and team-mate Charles Leclerc came close to boiling over. Antonelli drove a composed race amid some hectic action involving the other front-runners in a grand prix interrupted by a red flag that led to a 25-lap sprint to the finish. The Italian, a teenager until late August, spent the closing laps watching Hamilton try to get close enough to pass Verstappen after the two had made contact at the first chicane at the restart. But Hamilton found it impossible to get his Ferrari close enough to Verstappen to try to pass and ended the day frustrated and feeling a win had slipped through his fingers as a consequence of Leclerc's aggression on the first lap. That was a secondary story on the day Antonelli made history, smashing Sebastian Vettel's previous record for being the youngest champion by three years and 66 days. Antonelli also becomes the first Italian to win the F1 title since Alberto Ascari in 1953. Antonelli had tears mixed with laughter over the radio on the slowing down lap as he proved initially incapable of talking when his team told him he was world champion. After he half-composed himself, he said: "Thank you so much. We did it. We did it." A lap later, Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac crashed on lap 45 when its front suspension failed under braking for Turn One, leading initially to a safety car and then the race being stopped when it became clear how long it was going to take to repair the barriers. At the restart, Leclerc locked his left front wheel heavily as Verstappen and Hamilton battled for the lead in front of him, and Antonelli passed him at the start of the next lap. There was another safety car with 12 laps to go when Arvid Lindblad crashed his Racing Bulls after a collision with McLaren's Oscar Piastri. item.title: Eva Travis thrives in Wisconsin volleyball's win at UCLA | 3 takeaways
item.description: Wisconsin volleyball took care of business against another unranked opponent. The eighth-ranked Badgers bested UCLA in three sets, 25-22, 25-17, 25-17, on Nov. 1 at Pauley Pavilion in Los Angeles. It was UW’s 90th consecutive win against an unranked opponent in a streak that dates back to 2021. Here are three takeaways from the Badgers’ latter half of a 2-0 West Coast trip : Eva Travis shines in return to region Eva Travis, a native of Aliso Viejo, California, has played at an especially high level in her return to the Los Angeles area. After recording Wisconsin ’s last three kills in the Oct. 30 win over USC, Eva Travis had one of her best performances of the season against UCLA. Her 11 kills were second-best on the Badgers, trailing only Decelise Champion’s 15 kills. Travis did so without any attack errors – a first for her in Big Ten play – while hitting an exceptional .647. She also had four blocks and six digs. Travis now has recorded 10-plus kills in three of her last four matches. That includes her Michigan match with a .500 hitting percentage although she was much less efficient with an .083 hitting percentage against Washington. Badgers show blocking ability Wisconsin’s win over UCLA was one of its best of the season from a blocking standpoint. The Badgers had a 14-6 advantage in blocks in the three-set sweep. (Champion had a hand in eight of those 14 blocks.) UW had more blocks against the Bruins than against any of its previous 11 Big Ten opponents. The only match with more blocks was when UW had 17 blocks in a five-set win over then-No. 19 Texas A&M . UW had been averaging 2.12 blocks per set in its first 21 matches of the season before the 14 blocks in the three sets against UCLA. Wisconsin wins with Jaela Auguste on sideline Wisconsin’s uneventful sweep was without its 2025 third-team All-American on the court. Star middle blocker Jaela Auguste did not play against the Bruins. A team spokeswoman did not provide an update although the Big Ten Network broadcast said Auguste’s absence was a coach’s decision. Natalie Wardlow started in place of Auguste and finished with four kills, one attack error and a .375 hitting percentage. The sophomore was involved in six of UW’s 14 blocks. Wisconsin’s other starting middle blocker, Lynney Tarnow, had four kills without any attack errors and a .500 hitting percentage. She also finished with six blocks. Auguste has averaged 2.48 kills per set while hitting .398. She missed the Badgers’ matches against Stanford, Pittsburgh, Florida, Auburn and Texas A&M while dealing with an abdominal strain. item.title: Sebastian Vettel’s Message to Kimi Antonelli: ‘I Didn’t Sleep Properly for Days’
item.description: Sebastian Vettel congratulated Andrea Kimi Antonelli in a video message after the Italian broke his record to become F1’s youngest world champion, and warned him that he didn’t sleep properly for days after his own first title. After 71 laps in the F1 Mexico GP, Mercedes’ Antonelli claimed the 2026 drivers’ title by finishing third, surpassing four-time champion Vettel as the sport’s youngest-ever champion at 20 years, 68 days. He even got to share the podium with seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton and four-time champion Max Verstappen. It is a major achievement for Antonelli to get it done in only his second season in F1. He is the third champion from Italy and the first in 73 years. After a roller-coaster rookie season in 2025, the Italian bounced back well this year to take glory. He is the 36th driver to be crowned an F1 champion, and Formula 1 shared a recorded message for him from Vettel, who has often praised the Italian. Vettel recalled winning his first F1 title in 2010 with Red Bull and how he felt for days afterward. The Italian has revealed that they share texts often. Sebastian Vettel with Andrea Kimi Antonelli | Photo Credit: Mercedes F1 Team Vettel’s Message to F1 World Champion Antonelli “Kimi, congratulations. World champion, campione del mondo. Wow. Only very few of us managed to achieve that, and nobody has done it as young as you,” said Vettel. “You are curious, you listen, you learn fast, you are fearless. Your driving has been very clean and controlled, yet on the limit when it needed to be. “You understood that you can only control what you can control. I can try to get at least one point. You have a unique drive, and we enjoy watching you. When I won my first title, it all seemed to happen the moment I crossed the finish line. I was overwhelmed. I got out of the car, and the world around me was racing at full speed. “It was like a rush. It was impossible to reflect. I didn’t sleep properly for days, so be prepared. But I remember the feeling once it sank in, holding the world championship trophy in my hands and reading all the other champions’ names. I felt proud and satisfied. I realized the best part wasn’t crossing the line that decided the title. It was all the races that led up to it. “It is never the one race that matters. It is all the races we do. Every race shapes us. And with all that’s about to happen in the coming weeks, I’m sure you will soon feel the drive to race again, as in the bigger picture, there’s still a race to win. Lastly, a piece of advice. Great achievements might change the way people look at you, but you don’t have to change the way you look at people. Now go on and enjoy it. Un abbraccio forte, Sebastian. Ciao.” From Seb, to Kimi Passing on love, advice, and the youngest-ever champion record #F1 #MexicoGP https://t.co/L61c8R91QL — Formula 1 (@F1) November 1, 2026

item.title: NFL linebacker Campbell to remain hospitalized overnight
item.description: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell is carted off the field after being injured during the fourth quarter of an NFL victory by the Lions over Minnesota (Mike Mulholland) Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell was carted off the field and taken to a nearby hospital for overnight evaluation of a neck injury in Sunday's 19-15 NFL victory over previously unbeaten Minnesota. The Lions announced the details after Campbell was placed onto a backboard by medical personnel and driven off the field early in the fourth quarter, and the team later released an updated statement. "Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight, for continued evaluation and monitoring," the Lions said. "The team will provide further updates as we have them." Campbell was injured after making his third tackle of the contest by stopping Minnesota tight end TJ Hockenson. He was prone face down on the field and not moving. "Our thoughts and prayers are with Jack and his family," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said in his comments immediately after the game. "He's being taken care of. We don't have any new information. We'll keep you updated as this goes, but we're thinking about him." The 26-year-old from Iowa was a first-round selection in the 2023 NFL Draft by the Lions, chosen 18th overall. Campbell had a career-best season for Detroit in 2025 with 89 solo tackles, five sacks and 176 combined tackles. He also forced three fumbles and recovered two. "Jack's deal was definitely scary," Lions quarterback Jared Goff said. "It just brings you back to reality for a moment that he's a husband and a father. "Scary. We're praying for him and hope he's going to be all right. If anyone is tough enough to get through something like that, it's going to be him." The Lions signed Campbell last May to a four-year contract extension worth $81 million. js/amz

item.title: Angel City enters playoffs on a strong note by beating Boston
item.description: Sarah Gorden of Angel City FC dribbles the ball against Sarah Schupansky of Boston in the first half Sunday. (Katelyn Mulcahy / Getty Images) It has been a week since Angel City qualified for the NWSL playoffs. On Sunday, the team found out who and where it would be playing. With a 4-1 victory over Boston Legacy, Angel City finished the regular season fifth in the standings and will travel to Kansas City on Saturday to meet the Current in its second-ever trip to the postseason . And it will enter the playoffs as the hottest team in the NWSL, riding a league-best 10-game unbeaten streak. The goals Sunday came from Nealy Martin in the first half and Evelyn Shores, Sveindis Jonsdottir and Claire Emslie in the second. Boston’s only score came from Brazilian striker Amanda Gutierres just before intermission. Angel City began the final game of the regular season with a chance to finish as high as third in the table, earning the right to open the playoffs at home. But to do that it, it needed a win and it needed the two teams directly ahead of it, Kansas City and Washington, to lose. Neither the Current nor Spirit cooperated, leaving the standings mostly frozen where they were at the start of the week. Not that it really mattered, attacker Ally Sentnor said before the game. “You have to beat the best to win a championship. You have to beat everyone, so doesn’t really matter who you play at the beginning,” she said. “Every team in the playoffs is a great team, so I think we are just focused on us and what we’re doing on the field and what we are going to produce on the field. “We just take every game as it comes.” Read more: How Angel City found its stride and became one of the NWSL’s hottest teams Although Sunday’s match was a home game for Angel City (15-8-7), it wasn’t played at home. item.title: Cardinals Decline Option On Ryne Stanek
item.description: Jun 28, 2026; St. Louis, Missouri, USA; St. Louis Cardinals pitcher Ryne Stanek (55) throws in relief against the Miami Marlins in the seventh inning at Busch Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Tim Vizer-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Andrew Willis, Editor It was announced Sunday evening that the St. Louis Cardinals are declining the option on reliever Ryne Stanek . He had a $6 million option for 2027. Cardinals Decline Option On Ryne Stanek #stlcards are declining the team option on setup reliever Ryne Stanek’s contract, per source familiar with team’s decision. Stanek (RHP) becomes a free agent. He had a $6-million option for 2027. #Cardinals will go looking again for that veteran reliever (or two) like him. — Derrick Goold (@dgoold) November 1, 2026 Stanek, 35, pitched in 70 games for the Cardinals last season. He posted a 2-3 record alongside a 4.02 ERA. He pitched well overall. He had some months where he struggled , like in August when he posted a 4.91 ERA. On the other hand, he had three months where his ERA was 2.00 or lower. Cardinals Make Decision On Only Free Agent Ryne Stanek was the Cardinals’ only free agent this offseason. While the team likely considered picking up his option, they elected to not, which saves them $5 million (there was a $1 million buyout). Jul 19, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; St. Louis Cardinals pitcher Ryne Stanek (55) throws against the Arizona Diamondbacks in the sixth inning at Chase Field. Mandatory Credit: Rick Scuteri-Imagn Images What’s Next For the Cardinals? President of Baseball Operations Chaim Bloom will be looking to improve the bullpen for 2027. While there were plenty of bright spots, such as Riley O’Brien leading the league in saves, there were plenty of struggles . Bloom will likely look to sign a player or two similar to Stanek to solidify the bullpen. What’s Next For Ryne Stanek? Stanek pitched well enough in 2026 to have a job in 2027. A team looking to add a veteran righty can do with Stanek. Furthermore, they can do so at a reasonable price. Stanek will be on a MLB team in 2027. It is only a matter of which teams calls him. Main Photo: Tim Vizer- Imagn Images The Last Word Ryne Stanek provided the Cardinals with some effective innings. Given the shape of the bullpen as of now, and the possibility of an O’Brien trade , retaining Stanek would have made a great deal of sense. As it is, Bloom is choosing another direction. Teams can start signing free agents on Monday at 5:00 P.M. ET. The Cardinals’ bullpen could start taking shape rather quickly. item.title: Jack Campbell injury updates from Lions offer positive news on LB’s status
item.description: The NFL world was holding its breath during the Week 8 game between the Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings after linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a scary neck injury. Campbell was injured in the fourth quarter of the Lions’ win over the Vikings on Sunday and laid motionless on the field for several minutes before he was eventually loaded onto a stretcher and carted off the field. It was the kind of nightmare scene nobody ever wants to see for any person and all we could do was wait nervously for good news after the frightening situation. What made it even scarier was the reactions from players on both teams, including Lions star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson, who was understandably brought to tears. MORE: Vikings coach sends message after Jack Campbell’s scary injury Jack Campbell injury updates from Lions Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell and defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard check on linebacker Jack Campbell’s injury during the second half between Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Thankfully, we do have a few nuggets of good news, one of which came from Lions head coach Dan Campbell, who revealed that Jack Campbell was breathing and alert as he departed for the hospital. “He’s breathing, he’s alert when he left. I know nothing further. Thoughts and prayers are with Jack. I would ask that everyone does the same,” Campbell said , per Lions beat reporter Brad Galli. Not long after the Lions head coach’s update, the team revealed that Campbell is now resting at the local hospital he was transported to and the plan is to keep him overnight for “continued evaluation and monitoring.” “Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight, for continued evaluation and monitoring. The team will provide further updates as we have them,” the Lions said in a statement. MORE: 2026 NFL trade deadline tracker: Grading every deal, top available candidates Campbell’s injury occurred in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s contest when he attempted to make a tackle on Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson. So far, these are all positive developments considering the circumstances and how bad things looked initially. We can only hope there will continue to be good news on Campbell’s status moving forward and he no doubt has everyone’s thoughts and prayers. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Liverpool’s work in progress fizzles out in the face of streetwise champions | Andy Hunter
item.description: Afternoon began with talk of a title bid, but Arsenal looked more and more comfortable as the second half wore on Andoni Iraola had swatted aside any question that veered in the direction of Liverpool’s title credentials during his press conference on Friday with two simple words. “Too early,” he would respond. The Liverpool head coach was dismissive in terms of the stage of the season but, as Arsenal doggedly demonstrated, too early also applies to the development of his team. Arsenal cavorted to the sound of fury at Anfield. At the final whistle Mikel Arteta leapt into the arms of the first-team coach Gabriel Heinze as he celebrated the release of his first win at Liverpool as Arsenal manager, his club’s first league victory at Anfield in 14 years and the champions moving three points clear at the top of the table. His players, tireless in the protection of Kai Havertz’s early winner, lined up to accept the acclaim from a jubilant away section. Anger filled the space around them. Continue reading...

item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. Match-winner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project. Continue reading...

item.title: Arteta can take inspiration from George Graham to expunge painful Anfield memories
item.description: Arsenal have not won at Liverpool for 13 league games but Gunners’ win in 1989 remains one of club’s greatest nights Mikel Arteta used a Spanish word to describe what it felt like to be helpless at Anfield while playing for Everton in 2011: bajar . “It’s when a cyclist is going up and looks amazing, then in one kilometre he goes ‘boom’ and he’s struggling again,” he said in Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary. “The game was going well and then suddenly I could only see red shirts flying around. The game is passing all over me and I cannot react. I only had that feeling in my career once, and it was at Anfield.” Given Arteta’s record at Liverpool, Sunday’s showdown with his childhood friend Andoni Iraola – five days after Arsenal were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Fleetwood – could be expected to fill him with dread. Arteta finally tasted victory there as a player with Arsenal in September 2012 , after five failed attempts in the Merseyside derby, but ended up spending the night in hospital with concussion after colliding with Jordan Henderson in an incident he has described as “the biggest fear of my life”. item.description: After being dropped for ‘a breach of club discipline’, the winger must face the same questions about respect and self-awareness For the biggest game in Manchester City’s history, Jack Grealish was given a starting berth while Phil Foden, Julián Alvarez and Riyad Mahrez were on the bench. Grealish played the full 90 minutes of the Champions League triumph against Inter because Pep Guardiola had the greatest faith in the attacking midfielder, but three years on he is at risk of being yesterday’s man. That trust dwindled, not helped by injuries, and Grealish made only 17 Premier League starts over the next two seasons under Guardiola. City wanted him to leave in the summer of 2025, and Everton provided the solution, taking him on loan and borrowing him again for this season. item.title: Football Daily | Newcastle’s Jaissle wants to scream while Grealish leaves Moyes speechless
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While it is customary for fans of top-flight clubs with delusions of grandeur to cope with Fizzy Cup exits by pretending the competition is beneath them, this is no longer an option that is open to supporters of Newcastle United. Winning the trophy sponsored by a low-calorie, fruit-flavoured energy drink brand from Thailand may only rank fifth in the domestic pecking order behind the Premier League, FA Cup and both transfer windows, but nobody will ever forget how much it meant to hundreds of thousands of overjoyed Geordies when their team did exactly that the season before last to end a trophy drought dating back to the Jurassic era. And with a quarter-final trip to the tough-tackling League Two bullyboys of Fleetwood up for grabs during their match against serial trophy-dodgers Everton last night, the travelling Toon Army must have fancied their chances of being in the shake-up again. I clearly remember the first time I laughed out hard and loud, as a 12-year-old, reading Three Men in a Boat by Jerome K Jerome. Tonight, 50 years later, after a stretch of horrendous bad years and months (and for my mental health, I exclude the struggles of Tottenham), I read the Football Daily column. Its is often quite witty, but this time, reading about some penalty kick gone awry … I know, I have a simplistic sense of humour, but I laughed so hard and cried at the same time, that my family wondered what happened. Thanks for a cathartic experience. Words” – L Json. As a Spurs supporter who saw my first game at White Hart Lane when I was five years old – almost eight decades ago – I can only express my relief that attention has drifted away from the continual ridicule of my team. The fact that a certain club that should return to south of the Thames managed to lose at Highbury (ironically), that lot from down Kings Road and Manchester United are all hogging the headlines for all the wrong reasons just makes life sweeter. It’s time for my second nap of the day now, so I’ll sign off” – Stewart McGuinness. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
